_warum: Colors that BOTH UIs must keep identical. Web-App/public/tokens.css and Android-App/.../ui/theme/DesignTokens.kt are GENERATED from this file — do not edit either file by hand. See shared/README.md.

_notizen.chart-new: Chart colors — overridable per theme. Before, they were hard-coded in the JavaScript; no theme could adjust them, and in the brick look the amber of the used line stuck out of the otherwise blue palette.
_notizen.chart-used: In the brick theme sage green and sand — the same values as the condition badges .cond-new and .cond-used. The reason is not taste: everywhere in the UI these colors stand for exactly this distinction; whoever recognizes them in the chart does not have to read the legend. Before, it said --chart-used:#3d5a80 (the theme's primary color) — together with the light blue of the new line that made TWO shades of blue that only differed in lightness, and scaled down or printed such a difference is the first to disappear.
_notizen.brick-petrol: Action and value color of the brick theme. Exists only there — the base theme has no counterpart.
_notizen.ink: The edge of the theme "noppe" — border, offset shadow and text all use the same tone. Plastic casts no cloud, it rests on the surface: the shadow is the same tone as the border, only offset. With two tones the edge would look like a misprint.

_app_warum: Which constant of the app mirrors which token. The values are NOT here — they come from 'designs' above. This mapping generates DesignTokens.kt.
_listen_warum: Color series a theme ENUMERATES instead of naming them individually. They stand here and not in the themes above because their length belongs to the theme, not their role: the eleventh tone has no name of its own, it is simply the eleventh. From them --<praefix>-0..n in tokens.css and a listOf(...) in DesignTokens.kt are generated.

faecher.warum: The theme fan of the design "farbfaecher": twelve tones of equal lightness and chroma, only the hue changes — that way no theme stands out louder than another. The mapping is theme number modulo twelve. DELIBERATELY a fixed list instead of a calculation: a color formula would have to be rebuilt identically in CSS and in Kotlin, and exactly such pairs drift apart. A list can be generated.

steine.warum: The lid colors of the theme "noppe": six building brick tones the tile wall cycles through. They mean NOTHING — unlike the fan above, where the color is the theme. Here it gives rhythm, and that is exactly the catch of this theme: whoever knows the fan looks for information here that does not exist. Six and not twelve, so that the repetition stays readable as rhythm instead of chance. The mapping is the position in the list modulo six.

_erbt_warum: A theme can INHERIT the palette of another. "hochglanz" needs this: it is "noppe" as a glossy brochure — the same colors, plus layers (curvature, highlights, light streaks) that are not color values. Writing the eleven values down a second time would be a copy, and a copy does not follow along the next time.
_dunkel_warum: The dark variant PER theme, active with <html data-dunkel> (device choice “dark when the system is dark”). Before, whoever wanted dark got the theme “werkbank” — i.e. a different theme. 'basis' assigns surfaces, gray axis and status colors for all themes (the same roles as in themes/werkbank.css); per theme only the brand colors stand here, lightened so that text and lines in them stay readable on a dark background. Text on the brand color is then dark (--auf-primaer). Werkbank is already dark and has no variant. Both UIs read this section: the generator creates the dark blocks in public/tokens.css and the app table ui/theme/DunkelTokens.kt from it.
